messages:
Carla (PM): Heads-up: prototyping a new packaging idea — 'Route QoS Tokens' (RBQT). TL;DR: sell small bundles of per-route priority windows customers attach to specific API routes to reduce tail latency during spikes. Please flag concerns.

Ben (DevEx): Can we quantify what a token buys? hard SLA or probabilistic? how do we meter burn per-request?

Priya (Eng): Implementation notes: routing needs token-aware fast-path + token bucket. Option: token grants Xms of bypass for a route, or boosts priority in scheduler. Raises autoscaler/routing complexity though.

Amin (Sales): @Carla how is this different from 'priority lane' we already sell? customers want per-route control not account-wide. need positioning.

Elena (Legal): We should not promise strict uptime/SLOs unless capacity is reserved. Recommend marketing as "attempted priority" with fallbacks and clear contract language. Also mention burn caps and termination clauses.

Carla (PM): Agreed. Proposed scope: RBQT = ephemeral priority grants, no hard SLA, tokens have TTL and are consumed at request-time. Controls: per-account daily burn cap, per-token max qps uplift, attachable to single route or route group. Pricing prototype: example bundles + top-ups.

Ben (DevEx): Console needs: attach token to route, view remaining tokens, set auto-apply windows (e.g., deploys), and show historical priority events. Minimal UX for pilot.

Priya (Eng): Baseline feasibility: core tasks -> token store, O(1) routing check, metrics tagging + cost attribution. Rough estimate: 2-3 sprints to safe MVP (1 sprint for design/spec, 1-2 for infra + routing).

Amin (Sales): Sales angle: call it 'per-route emergency credits' for now. Customers likely want monthly bundles + one-off. Suggested shelf price for discussion: 100 tokens = $250, token gives ~100ms tail-latency protection up to configured uplift.

Carla (PM): Draft SKU snippet (for discussion):

```
sku_id: RBQT-001
name: "Route QoS Token Pack"
units: tokens
bundle: 100
price_usd: 250
ttl_days: 30
per_token_effect: "priority boost / up to 2x qps uplift 
apply_to: route_id(s)
```

Ben (DevEx): Also need example contract language for workshops/pilot: soft start, non-binding performance indicators, clear recourse.

Elena (Legal): I'll draft T&Cs: no hard latency SLA, refund triggers only if platform-wide regression, require customer to maintain reasonable usage patterns. Also add audit log requirements for enterprise pilots.

Priya (Eng): Security note: emit audit events from routing layer. KMS/HSM not required unless the token is used to gate access to private models — then we need tighter controls.

Ben (DevEx): Ops ask: run a simulation on a realistic spike pattern to measure cost and capacity impact. @ops-bot can you queue a sim?

ops-bot: Queued sim job #4721 for RBQT pilot scenario. ETA ~3h. Will post results to thread when complete.

Carla (PM): Next steps: Priya + Ben -> tech spec; Elena -> draft T&Cs; Amin -> identify 2-3 pilot customers and pitch angle; I'll consolidate into PRD by EOD Friday. :rocket:
